headline: Meta's AI team engineers call it a gulag amid layoffs and morale issues
summary: Meta's Applied AI team of 6,500 face low morale and 'soul-crushing' work
details: Meta's Applied AI team, formed three months ago with 6,500 engineers and product managers, faces low morale and 'soul-crushing' work. Employees describe being forced into the group with little choice, tasked with generating puzzles and coding problems to train AI models.

A recent incident involved a hijacked livestreamed presentation with an expletive-laden outburst, reflecting simmering rage within the team. Over 1,600 Meta employees have signed a petition protesting a program monitoring their clicks and keystrokes for AI training data.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg addressed the situation in an internal memo, acknowledging recent changes had 'caused distress' and admitting the company made mistakes. He emphasized Meta's goal to be 'the best place for the most talented people in the world to make an impact'.

The team is led by Maher Saba, previously a vice president in Meta's Reality Labs division, and reports to CTO Andrew Bosworth. Originally, the team was structured with up to 50 employees per manager.
caption:
Is Meta's AI push causing employee burnout? 6,500 engineers face 'soul-crushing' work

Meta's Applied AI team, formed three months ago with 6,500 engineers and product managers, faces low morale and 'soul-crushing' work. Employees describe being forced into the group with little choice, tasked with generating puzzles and coding problems to train AI models.

A recent incident involved a hijacked livestreamed presentation with an expletive-laden outburst, reflecting simmering rage within the team. Over 1,600 Meta employees have signed a petition protesting a program monitoring their clicks and keystrokes for AI training data.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg addressed the situation in an internal memo, acknowledging recent changes had 'caused distress' and admitting the company made mistakes. He emphasized Meta's goal to be 'the best place for the most talented people in the world to make an impact'.

The team is led by Maher Saba, previously a vice president in Meta's Reality Labs division, and reports to CTO Andrew Bosworth. Originally, the team was structured with up to 50 employees per manager.
